root_cause_label: Frequency-only shape selection omits global maximum aligned seq_align (2048), causing infeasible plans where seq_align < aligned prompt_len for large prompts throughout the entire tail of the trajectory.
one_sentence_failure_summary: At step 15 the agent switches to frequency-only shape selection, permanently dropping the required maximum aligned shape (2048) from the representative set, so all subsequent plans assign large prompts to undersized shapes and never meet bucket 1 performance thresholds.
t_err_evidence: Step 15 implements optimized_packer.py with choose_optimal_shapes() that selects only the 8 most-frequent seq_aligns [64,128,192,256,320,384,512,576], dropping the global maximum aligned prompt length (2048). This is the first step where the maximum shape is absent from the representative set, violating the constraint seq_align >= ceil(prompt_len/64)*64 for requests with prompt_len near 2048.
t_commit_evidence: Every packer written from step 15 onward (optimized_packer, final_packer_fixed, complete_packer, target_packer, final_optimized_packer, final_tuned_packer, precision_packer, final_solution, ultimate_solution, optimal_final) uses the same choose_best_shapes() function selecting top-frequency shapes, never re-introducing the max shape. The agent never diagnoses the root cause as missing max coverage, so the outcome is locked in.
t_surface_evidence: Step 16 evaluation output shows 'Shapes used: [(64, 32, 4096), (128, 32, 4096), (320, 32, 4096), (384, 32, 4096), (512, 32, 4096), (576, 32, 4096)]' for bucket 1, with the maximum at 576 rather than 2048. The shapes conspicuously lack any shape at or above 2048, signaling infeasible coverage, but the agent does not react to this signal.
trigger_explanation: At step 15 the agent acts on the false premise that selecting the most-frequent seq_align values is sufficient for a valid plan, without verifying that the shape set must cover the global maximum aligned prompt length. The agent's reasoning focuses only on minimizing compilation cost by picking high-frequency shapes, ignoring the feasibility invariant that every request's seq_align assignment must be >= its own aligned prompt length.
forewarning_evidence: Step 14 evaluation of the improved_packer (which did include 2048) shows 'Shapes used: [(64, 32, 4096), (128, 32, 4096), (320, 32, 4096), (512, 32, 4096), (576, 32, 4096), (2048, 32, 4096)]' -- the presence of 2048 was an implicit signal that it was needed to cover the large-prompt requests. Immediately after, step 15 drops 2048 without investigating the effect.
